references.text: The scouts came to the Valley of Eshkol and cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which they carried on a pole between them. This is the original account of the Valley of Eshkol referred to here.
The scouts gave a negative report about the land and discouraged the people so that they did not want to enter the land.
The people lost heart and wept all night after the scouts' negative report, and they wished to return to Egypt.
The scouts who brought an evil report about the land and caused the congregation to grumble died by a plague before the Lord.
Moses recounts the story of the scouts who came to the Valley of Eshkol and how the people lost heart and did not want to enter the land.
The psalmist describes how the Israelites despised the pleasant land and did not believe in the Lord's word, but grumbled in their tents.
Hebrews refers to the generation that rebelled after hearing the scouts' report and was not allowed to enter the rest because of unbelief.
